# casdoor_subscription (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor subscription of a user to a plan.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_subscription" "alice" {
  owner        = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  name         = "sub-alice"
  display_name = "Alice - Pro"
  user         = casdoor_user.alice.name
  pricing      = casdoor_pricing.default.name
  plan         = casdoor_plan.pro_monthly.name
  period       = "Monthly"
  start_time   = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  end_time     = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  state        = "Active"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the subscription, unique within its owner.
- `owner` (String) The organization that the object belongs to.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description.
- `display_name` (String) The display name.
- `end_time` (String) The time when the subscription ends, in the RFC 3339 format.
- `payment` (String) The name of the payment.
- `period` (String) The billing period, `Monthly` or `Yearly`.
- `plan` (String) The name of the plan.
- `pricing` (String) The name of the pricing.
- `start_time` (String) The time when the subscription starts, in the RFC 3339 format.
- `state` (String) The state: `Pending`, `Error`, `Suspended`, `Active`, `Upcoming` or `Expired`.
- `user` (String) The name of the user.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the subscription was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the subscription in the `owner/name` format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the organization and the name.
terraform import casdoor_subscription.example <organization>/<name>
```
